stem: A gym offers two membership plans. Plan A has a one-time joining fee of 40 dollars plus 25 dollars per month. Plan B has no joining fee and costs \(k\) dollars per month. For a membership of 7 or fewer whole months, Plan B costs less than Plan A, and for a membership of 8 or more whole months, Plan B costs more than Plan A. Which of the following could be the value of \(k\)?
solution: For \(m\) months, Plan B costs more than Plan A when \(km > 25m + 40\), that is, when \((k - 25)m > 40\).
This must be false for \(m = 7\) and true for \(m = 8\): \(7(k - 25) < 40 < 8(k - 25)\), so \(5 < k - 25 < \frac{40}{7}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. With \(k = 31\), a 7-month membership costs 217 dollars on Plan B and 215 dollars on Plan A, so Plan B already costs more at 7 months.
explanation.B: Correct. \(7(30.5) = 213.5 < 215\) and \(8(30.5) = 244 > 240\), and the gap only widens after that.
explanation.C: Incorrect. With \(k = 30\), both plans cost 240 dollars for 8 months, so Plan B does not cost more at 8 months.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With \(k = 29\), an 8-month membership costs 232 dollars on Plan B and 240 dollars on Plan A, so Plan B still costs less at 8 months.
